principle: High-rep pump sets (about 7 sets x 8-12 reps, 30-45s rest) performed at the END of a target-muscle session, aiming for maximal blood-flow pump on the last exercise trained for that muscle.
constraints: Avoid for complete beginners (experienceLevel BEGINNER or UNKNOWN)
Avoid when painScore/safetyFlags indicate joint pain
Only ever offered as an optional finisher, never a required part of the base program
contraindications: acute joint pain in the target muscle/joint
usage_in_app: Optional finisher suggestion for a lagging body part (findLaggingMuscleGroups output), gated by experienceLevel === ADVANCED and safetyFlags.severity !== critical
wording_rule: Present as 'kỹ thuật finisher lấy cảm hứng từ nguyên tắc FST-7 công khai' — never 'lịch tập FST-7 của Hany Rambod'

principle: Structure a single session in 3 phases: (1) pre-activation with moderate weight, 8-12 reps, no intensity techniques; (2) strength/tension phase working up to a hard-but-controlled top set; (3) pump phase using intensity techniques (drop-sets, rest-pause) only on isolation/accessory work at the end.
constraints: Avoid phase 3 (drop-sets/rest-pause) for beginner or unknown experience level
Avoid phase 3 additions when fatigueScore is high or recoveryScore is low
Phase 1/2 (no intensity techniques) remain safe defaults for any level
usage_in_app: Optional session-structure template for ADVANCED users choosing a Bro Split / Specialization Block
wording_rule: Present as 'cấu trúc buổi tập lấy cảm hứng từ nguyên tắc Mountain Dog công khai' — never attribute a specific workout as John Meadows' own program

source_ref: Dr. Layne Norton — PHAT (Power Hypertrophy Adaptive Training)
principle: Train each major muscle group twice per week within a 5-day split: 2 'power' days (low reps, heavy load, powerlifting-style) and 3 'hypertrophy' days (higher reps, higher volume, bodybuilding-style) covering the same muscle groups.
constraints: Requires at least INTERMEDIATE experienceLevel — the twice-weekly heavy+high-volume combination is a meaningful fatigue load
Not recommended when adherenceRate is already struggling to meet a simpler 3-4 day split
Power-day top sets should be gated by RPE/RIR reliability — see docs/gym-fitness-research.md §3 on autoregulation accuracy by experience level
usage_in_app: Optional template suggestion for INTERMEDIATE/ADVANCED users wanting combined strength+hypertrophy goals
wording_rule: Present as 'mẫu lịch lấy cảm hứng từ nguyên tắc Power/Hypertrophy công khai (PHAT-inspired)' — never 'chương trình PHAT chính thức của Layne Norton'

method: Renaissance Periodization inspired mesocycle + deload structure
principle: Structure training in ~4-week mesocycles with volume increasing week to week (volume-first linear progression), followed by a deload week (reduced volume/intensity) before the next mesocycle begins.
constraints: The 4-week/1-deload cadence is a product default informed by practitioner consensus and Bell et al. (2025) 4-8 week deload guidance — not a fixed medical rule; adjust per data (see docs/TRAINING_CYCLE_DECISION_ENGINE.md)
For BEGINNER users, deload triggers should stay conservative/infrequent — beginners rarely accumulate enough fatigue to need one in a first 4-week block
usage_in_app: Backing rationale for cycle-thresholds.config.ts's minimumCycleDays=28 default and the DELOAD decision branch's cadence expectations
wording_rule: Present as 'cấu trúc chu kỳ lấy cảm hứng từ nguyên tắc mesocycle/deload công khai' — never attribute to a specific paid RP program
